statement: Intel is expanding capacity behind an improving foundry, raising its capital expenditure plan to more than $20 billion and ramping 18A with better yields while foundry losses narrowed.
why: More capex and a maturing leading-edge process widen the pool of non-TSMC, non-Nvidia capacity available to AI buyers over the next few years.

impact.mechanism: Rising capex and an improving in-house leading-edge process add alternative manufacturing supply, easing the single-source bottleneck for AI silicon.

evidence.source: Intel Newsroom / Intel Q2 2026 earnings release
evidence.excerpt: capital expenditure plan raised to $20+ billion (up about $3 billion); AI-driven businesses grew more than 70% YoY and represent about 70% of revenue; 18A process ramping with improving yields; 14A high-volume manufacturing targeted for 2028

confidence.basis: Secondary relay of company statements; capacity and yield claims are self-reported and not independently verified here.
